summary.text: A 49-year-old woman with recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, IgA nephropathy and severe mucocutaneous disorders, height 152 cm, weight 33.5 kg and albumin 1.9 g/dL, had begun hemodialysis via central venous catheterization 7 years previously and was converted to peritoneal dialysis 4 years before after repeated catheterizations damaged her central veins. She needed peritoneal dialysis catheter replacement.

Preoperative evaluation showed Mallampati class IV, limited mouth opening and severe oral adhesion; general anesthesia was deemed problematic and neuraxial anesthesia was precluded by a skin lesion at the potential puncture site, so ultrasound-guided subcostal TAPB was planned as the primary analgesia modality.

After monitors were fitted and fentanyl 25 μg, ketamine 5 mg and propofol target-controlled infusion were given, left-sided ultrasound-guided subcostal TAPB was performed with 20 mL of 0.5% lidocaine with epinephrine using a gel and no-sliding probe technique. Surgery began after loss of cold sensation from T7 to T12 was confirmed in the left anterior abdominal wall.

The original catheter was removed and a new catheter placed in the left abdominal wall. Moderate pain at incision point A on the non-blocked side and mild pain at point D on the blocked side were managed with additional lidocaine, intravenous fentanyl and ketamine; repeated low-dose fentanyl was given for peritoneal manipulation without visceral pain. Anesthesia lasted 128 min (total fentanyl 200 μg, ketamine 50 mg, 1% lidocaine 4.4 mL) without serious respiratory depression, unbearable pain or other serious complication, and she later reported considerably less pain than at the initial catheter placement.
